title: FA Demands Infantino Documents on World Cup Sale
seoTitle: FA Demands Infantino Docs on World Cup Sale & Governance
subtitle: Debbie Hewitt Calls for Transparency on FFE Plan and Balogun's Suspension
excerpt: FA Chair Debbie Hewitt has formally requested FIFA President Gianni Infantino to provide all documents concerning the World Cup sale plan and a ban suspension.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Football Association (FA) Chair Debbie Hewitt has sent a letter to FIFA President Gianni Infantino, demanding all documents relating to the World Cup sale plan and the lifting of Folarin Balogun's ban. The message, also sent to FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström, highlights governance failures and the need for an independent review of the FFA's conception and the decision to suspend Balogun's ban.

What Prompted Hewitt's Letter

Hewitt, who serves as a FIFA Vice President, stated that the FIFA Council should receive a written explanation regarding the cancelled suspension of Folarin Balogun's ban, which allowed the United States striker to participate in the match against Belgium in the last 16. The original suspension, stemming from a red card in a match against Bosnia and Herzegovina, was suspended for a year without clear justification, merely citing a rule that permits the suspension of penalties.

The FFE Plan and the Crisis of Confidence

The FFE (FIFA Forward Enterprise) plan envisioned the creation of a new company to manage the commercial and ticketing rights for all competitions, including the World Cups, with 21% of the shares to be sold to a private investment firm. The project was aborted after criticism from several federations. UEFA, Concacaf, and the AFC issued an open letter accusing FIFA of “deception” and “lack of confidence” in the plan.

FIFA's Reaction and the Political Dispute

In response, FIFA accused UEFA of a “defamatory campaign” against the organization. Infantino, 56, is running for a fourth term in March, while Council members have until November 18 to put forward an alternative candidate. FIFA has not yet communicated with the Council about the FFE plan, but the meeting on October 15 in Zurich is the first since the project emerged in July.

Impact on Bidding Choices and the Women's World Cup

The FA's stance on the matter carries risk, as the United Kingdom is the sole candidate for the 2035 Women's World Cup. The decision on the hosts for the 2031 and 2035 editions will be made at an extraordinary FIFA congress on November 23. The FA's initial letter of support for Infantino was withdrawn after the controversies emerged.

Next Steps for Transparency

Infantino must make all documents available before the Council meeting on October 15. Hewitt's letter also calls for an independent review of who conceived the FFE and how the private offer was submitted for bidding. The expectation is that the discussion will address not only the FFE but also FIFA's response to the crisis generated by this controversy.

With information from BBC, The Guardian.
